text: Compared with natural deduction, a Hilbert-style proof system is characterized by:
choices: many inference rules (intro/elim for each connective) and no axioms
sequents of the form Γ ⊢ Δ together with structural rules
a tree-based refutation search that requires no creativity
a few axiom schemas plus a single inference rule (modus ponens)
explanation: A Hilbert system uses a small set of axiom schemas (typically 3–4) and just one rule, modus ponens — minimal but hard for humans. Option 1 describes natural deduction (rules, essentially no axioms), option 2 describes the sequent calculus, and option 3 describes semantic tableaux.
